reconcile.connective: Commentators read the 'treasures of the snow' as figurative — God's readiness to act, not a literal stockpile — leaving Ecclesiastes' naturalistic water-cycle picture untouched.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (Steve Wells) flags Job 38:22's literal snow-and-hail warehouses as scientific absurdity next to Ecclesiastes' commonsense water cycle.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com), entry on Job 38:22 (labeled Absurdity/Science/Contradiction)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The idea in Job 38:22 is not that - as for instance the peasants of Menn, four hours' journey from Damascus, garner up the winter snow in a cleft of the rock, in order to convey it to Damascus and the towns of the coast in the hot months - God treasures up the snow and hail above to cause it to descend according to opportunity.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly denies that Job 38:22's 'treasures' describe a literal stockpile, defusing the charge that the verse presents a naive storehouse cosmology at odds with Ecclesiastes' naturalistic water-cycle language.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Now we are not to imagine that the Lord has stores of these laid up in heaps, in times past for time to come; but that he can and does as easily and as soon produce them when he pleases, as one that has treasures laid up can bring them forth at once.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly rejects a literal warehouse reading of 'treasures,' reading the verse as a figure for God's power rather than a rival cosmology to Ecclesiastes' water cycle.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The treasures of the snow - The places where snow is formed, and the cause of that formation.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Glosses 'treasures' as ordinary meteorological locations (where snow forms) rather than a supernatural stockpile, aligning the verse with natural-process language.

pd_work.resource: C. F. Keil and F. Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-1875), on Job 38:22
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this exact verse directly, denying a literal storehouse and calling the design of the divine speech 'ethical, not scientific' — a harmonizing commentator already surfaced on the row.
